claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The proposed model uses physically derived microstructure descriptors obtained from targeted coarse-grained simulations and limited experiments.
A machine-learning surrogate can predict mechanical properties, including yield strength, from alloy features.
The proposed framework can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness for hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework will be faster and more accurate than traditional DFT- or CALPHAD-based methods.
The prediction method is intended for ambient-temperature testing with the hierarchical microstructure preserved.
Reliable predictions require microstructure descriptors obtained under controlled and reproducible conditions.
Multilevel chemical fluctuations and associated microstructural features mediate the relationship between composition and mechanical properties.
Physical constraints derived from coarse-grained simulations guide the learning process.
Physics-informed learning enables the model to capture key microstructure-property relationships.
Machine-learning models can reduce dependence on computationally intensive strict calculations and accelerate alloy-property screening.
The proposed framework will reduce average prediction errors for Young's modulus, yield strength, and toughness by roughly 30% relative to existing methods.
The proposed framework will reduce computational demands by at least one order of magnitude.
DFT and physically based mechanical-property calculations can require extensive or lengthy computation.
Traditional DFT, CALPHAD, and standard regression baselines have higher prediction errors than the proposed model.
The model's advantage may cease when phase transformations, degradation, or other changes move the hierarchical microstructure outside its calibrated domain.
The model may cease to be reliable when its input microstructure descriptors cannot be extracted reliably.
The estimated gains depend on the quality and representativeness of the microstructure descriptors.
A blinded prospective comparison will measure predictions and standardized tensile and fracture-test results on multiple HfNbTiVAl10 samples and compare them with conventional-method predictions.
The hypothesis is declared falsified only if the model fails both the 30% error-reduction target and the tenfold computational-resource-reduction target across a statistically significant test set.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome promises both a roughly 30% error reduction and at least a tenfold resource reduction, but the falsification rule requires failure of both targets. Thus, failure of either promised gain alone would not falsify the hypothesis, making the rule weaker than the stated prediction.
